writeup: TIC 469305326 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system with an orbital period of 3.3470 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 4.01% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal shows strong statistical significance with a BLS detection signal-to-noise ratio of 221.6. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 31.6, though the centroid offset of 2.1 arcsec warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel finding. The machine learning screening score of 0.32 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing system rather than instrumental noise or other artifacts.
